name: OR-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by six points on the 2024 baseline
Salinas is an incumbent with a large fundraising edge
Republican challenger has raised almost nothing
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Salinas: a Democratic-leaning district, incumbency, and a dominant money advantage over a challenger who has raised under $13,000. Prediction markets agree, pricing her near 96%, so the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Salinas or an unusually strong Republican wave environment could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Oregon's 6th District leans Democratic, and first-term incumbent Andrea Salinas is running for reelection with the advantages that come with it. She has raised about $1.6 million and holds over $600,000 in cash, while Republican David Russ has raised under $13,000 with almost nothing banked. No outside groups are currently opposing her, and no independent polls of the race are available.

With no expert ratings or polling to lean on, the forecast rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which price the Democrat around 96 percent. The race is rated Safe Democratic, though the absence of polling keeps uncertainty somewhat elevated.
